subject: Order Form Annex — anchored discount, true-up & revenue shelf edits (Exhibit S)
messages:
From: Emily Hart <emily.hart@pinebridgehealth.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pinebridgehealth.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit S redlines — discount smoothing + revenue shelf proposal

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are Pinebridge's proposed redlines to Exhibit S (pricing schedule) and a short spreadsheet that shows how the smoothing would work across our expected monthly consumption profile. High level asks:

- Add a 6-month "anchored discount" where the customer's effective discount rate floors at 8% for months 1–6 if monthly committed usage dips below the tier threshold.
- Introduce a "revenue shelf" credit that accrues when usage is above target and can be applied against future shortfalls (we proposed a 12-month shelf).
- Limit any retroactive true-up credits to 30% of the monthly committed fee per month (we put this in the redlines).

We highlighted the clauses we changed in the attached PDF (Pinebridge_Redlines_ExhibitS.pdf). Can Redwood share a marker where you would accept the anchored discount but retain a hard cap on credits?

Would appreciate a call tomorrow morning to walk through — inventory open next-day slots?

Best,
Emily
Emily Hart
Head of Procurement, Pinebridge Health
[Attachment: Pinebridge_Redlines_ExhibitS.pdf]

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@pinebridgehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit S redlines — discount smoothing + revenue shelf proposal

Emily — thanks for the detailed markups and the spreadsheet, very clear. I put an internal draft of an annex attached that tries to preserve your intent while protecting Redwood against an unbounded credit exposure. Key points from our side:

- We can accept an anchored discount for the first 6 months, provided the anchored discount is scoped to a per-month cap (proposed: 20% of that month's committed fee).
- For the revenue shelf: we can support a 12-month shelf, but credits would expire after 12 months and be limited to an aggregate cap equal to 25% of total committed spend in the 12-month period.
- We're proposing the true-up window be 45 days (instead of 90), which reduces open accounting risk for us and keeps forecasting clean.

I copied Karthik and Lauren to weigh in on pricing mechanics and A/R implications. Attaching Proposed_Annex_v3.docx for internal redline; I'll send a cleaned PDF to you after we align internally.

Can you confirm Pinebridge's target month where the shelf would start (is it billing month when usage exceeds target or calendar month end)? That determines the accrual timing.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_Annex_v3.docx]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 12:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exhibit S redlines — discount smoothing + revenue shelf proposal

Agree with Mateo's framing. A few pricing mechanics to consider before we send a counter:

1) Anchored discount: make it explicit that the "anchor" applies only to committed-token tiers and does not cascade to overage pricing.
2) Shelf accrual: we should accelerate the shelf recognition to the next invoice cycle but limit total shelf applied per invoice to 30% of that invoice's committed fee. This prevents a large offset in a single month.
3) Credit cap: set an absolute annualized cap (e.g., 25% of annual committed spend) rather than a rolling percent to simplify forecasting for finance.

If legal signs off on the 45-day true-up and the wording around "expiration/forfeit of shelf credits", we can aim to accept the main commercial ask. Soojin, any redline language you'd prefer for the credit expiration clause?

Karthik
VP, Revenue Operations

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Legal notes — Exhibit S redline review

Team — quick legal read of Emily's attachments and Mateo's proposed annex. Summary of recommended edits (attaching legal redline):

- Replace "floor" terminology with "Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC)" to avoid ambiguity between contractual minimums and accounting floors.
- Constrain the revenue shelf credit: credits accrue only when monthly usage exceeds the committed tier by >5% and are automatically forfeited if not applied within 12 months from accrual date.
- Change true-up window from 90 to 45 days (as Mateo proposed). If Procurement insists on 90, propose a mid-point of 60 days but require a timely reconciliation covenant to avoid stale credits.
- Add a hard cap: total credits applied in any 12-month period shall not exceed 25% of total committed fees for that period. Explicitly exclude passthrough costs from the calculation.
- Add audit rights: customer can request usage detail once per quarter; Redwood will provide within 15 business days.

I've attached Legal_Redline_AnnexS_v2.docx with inline language we can propose back to Pinebridge. Two open policy items for commercial: whether the shelf applies to overage invoices (recommended: no) and whether we allow stitching of credits to renewals (recommended: yes, only at renewal with a one-time apply).

— Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Legal_Redline_AnnexS_v2.docx]

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@pinebridgehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit S redlines — discount smoothing + revenue shelf proposal

Emily — thank you again for the fast turn. We've reviewed your redlines internally and propose the following counterpoints (summary):

- Anchored discount: we can accept a 6-month anchored discount but must limit the per-month anchored discount to 20% of that month's committed fee. This keeps the uplift bounded for Redwood while giving Pinebridge the smoothing you asked for.
- Revenue shelf: we'll support a 12-month accrual shelf, credits expire 12 months from accrual, and aggregate credits applied in any rolling 12-month window cannot exceed 25% of committed spend for that window. Credits will not apply to overage charges.
- True-up: propose 45 days. If Pinebridge cannot meet that cadence, we can consider 60 days as a concession if Pinebridge accepts a modest increase to the credit cap.
- Audit & reconciliation: we'll provide usage detail on request (quarterly limit) with 15 business days turnaround.

We've attached a legal-marked draft (Legal_Redline_AnnexS_v2.docx) with the language Soojin recommended. Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00am PT to finalize the framing and then have legal exchange the signed redline? If that time doesn't work, offer another slot and we'll make it work.

Looking forward to closing this quickly — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
